Lecture 1.Title: Introduction
Lecture 1.Description: Covered class agenda, syllabus, tools used in class, group project, and expectations moving forward.

Lecture 2.Title: The Basics
Lecture 2.Description: Covered servers, URIs/URLs, IP addresses, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, SSL certificates, HTTP methods and status codes, idempotence, and the three-tier model.

Lecture 3.Title: CSS Part 1
Lecture 3.Description: Covered CSS anatomy, selectors, tags, attributes, attribute/pseudo selectors, formatting, display, visibility, box model, positioning, and inheritance.

Lecture 4.Title: CSS Part 2
Lecture 4.Description: Covered CSS combinators, animations, minification, and bootstrap.

Lecture 5.Title: JavaScript
Lecture 5.Description: Covered what JS is, how it's useful, and adding it to sites. Then, went over comments, objects, variables, values, operators, control structures, and functions. Finally, reviewed DOM and event handling.

Lecture 6.Title: AJAX & JSON
Lecture 6.Description: Covered basic JSON structure (Collections and Arrays), all possible JSON values, and parsing it. Then, covered what AJAX is and how to use basic jQuery functions alongside it. Finally, covered how to use XMLHttpRequest.

Lecture 7.Title: APIs
Lecture 7.Description: Covered API definition, SOAP, and REST. For REST, went over the 6 constraints (universal interface, stateless, cacheable, client-server, layered system, and code on demand). Then, looked at some real-world API examples.

Lecture 8.Title: Front End Optimizations
Lecture 8.Description: Covered how to measure/care about performance, efficient/minimizing markups, having CSS at the top of the page, JavaScript after HTML, ETags, Expires headers, Image Sprites, CDNs, event delegation, GET instead of POST, polling, and the 7 key factors of UX design.

Lab 1.Title: Portfolio Website
Lab 1.Description: Created a group portfolio page that included team name, slogan, logo, and previous works. Also created individual resume pages and implemented some hCard microformat conventions on contact information.

Lab 2.Title: Constitution Day Lab
Lab 2.Description: Created an interactive Constitution website and did analysis on Articles I-VII and Ammendments 1-10.

Lab 3.Title: JavaScript, AJAX, JSON, using APIs
Lab 3.Description: Connected to the OpenWeatherMap API and one other API and created interactive websites about information they both provide.

Lab 4.Title: Lab 3 with AI
Lab 4.Description: Remade our Lab 3 using only AI-generated code, images, text, etc. Logged our prompt usage in our README file.

Lab 5.Title: Bloomberg Terminal
Lab 5.Description: Experimented on many different functions and features of the Bloomberg Terminals and wrote a one-page reflection on it in Part 1. In Part 2, wrote a one-page summary of integrating its financial data onto class projects.

Lab 6.Title: PHP, OOP, and Input Handling
Lab 6.Description: Created a basic calculator using PHP and worked on classes/subclasses of Addition, Multiplication, Subtraction, and Division.
